public_partners.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
public_partners.description: The primary U.S. government environmental agency, managing the three Superfund sites in St. Louis. Region 5 (Chicago); Project Manager Thomas Alcamo, alcamo.thomas@epa.gov, (312) 886-7278.

public_partners.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
public_partners.description: Monitors public health risks related to Superfund projects.

public_partners.name: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR)
public_partners.description: CDC division funded under Superfund to conduct health assessments at contaminated sites.

public_partners.name: National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS)
public_partners.description: Part of the National Institutes of Health; works on health research related to environmental exposure.

public_partners.name: International Joint Commission (IJC)
public_partners.description: The Canada–U.S. Great Lakes agency, established in 1909, overseeing boundary waters; has attended Task Force meetings.

public_partners.name: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE)
public_partners.description: State equivalent to the EPA; assumes Superfund site monitoring after cleanup.

public_partners.name: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS)
public_partners.description: Addresses contamination exposures and manages the Michigan PBB Registry for exposed populations.

public_partners.name: Mid-Michigan District Health Department (Gratiot County Office)

private_stakeholders.name: Michigan Chemical / Velsicol
private_stakeholders.description: Founded 1935 in St. Louis; produced DDT during WWII, later expanded into flame retardants (PBB) and rare earth processing. Acquired by Velsicol Chemical (Chicago) in 1965, later owned by Northwest Industries/Fruit of the Loom. Dumped large quantities of DDT waste, radioactive residue, and PBB into the local environment.

private_stakeholders.name: Oxford Automotive (Lobdell-Emery)
private_stakeholders.description: Auto parts manufacturer in eastern Alma. Discharged hexavalent chromium and potentially PFAS through storm drains into Pine River tributaries. Filed bankruptcy and closed in 2004.

private_stakeholders.name: Total Energies / Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (UDS) / Valero
private_stakeholders.description: Oil refineries that operated on Alma's east side, discharging refinery wastes into the Pine River and releasing VOCs, heavy metals, and acids into air and water. Total closed in 1999.

private_stakeholders.name: Jacobs Engineering Group
private_stakeholders.description: Prime EPA contractor for Superfund site remediation — not a polluter.

private_stakeholders.name: Weston Solutions
private_stakeholders.description: Provides technical assistance to Michigan EGLE; headquartered in West Chester, PA.

college_university_partners.name: Alma College
college_university_partners.description: The four-year liberal arts college in Alma, about four miles from the Velsicol Superfund sites in St. Louis. Students and faculty have volunteered on contamination issues and shared the 2008 Jimmy & Rosalynn Carter Partnership Award with the Task Force.

college_university_partners.name: Central Michigan University
college_university_partners.description: Faculty and students have worked on watershed contamination projects. Houses Task Force records at the Clarke Historical Library, and is home to WCMU Public Media, the PBS/NPR regional affiliate.

college_university_partners.name: Emory University, Rollins School of Public Health
college_university_partners.description: Has maintained the PBB Registry since 2011, providing technical assistance on exposure documentation and health studies related to contamination.

college_university_partners.name: Michigan State University
college_university_partners.description: Engaged in environmental and health research on watershed impacts. MSU Press has published books on regional contamination, and MSU co-hosted the 50th anniversary celebration of Silent Spring with Alma College in 2012.

college_university_partners.name: University of Michigan
college_university_partners.description: Pioneered early fish-kill studies (1935) and toxicity analysis of PBB following the 1973 accident. Continues research on persistent pollutants including PFAS.
